claims.statement: Cite-Right 0.4.0 ships an optional native extension at cite_right._core that reimplements prepare, the inverted index, and Smith-Waterman alignment in Rust, published as abi3 wheels (abi3-py311) including linux/aarch64 plus an sdist.

The default / Rust path is index-first: the inverted index chooses which source windows are worth aligning, and Smith-Waterman still localizes char_start / char_end on the selected windows plus any embedding extras.

PreparedCitationCorpus.from_sources takes the Rust prepare path only when use_rust=True (default), cite_right._core imports successfully, the tokenizer is a SimpleTokenizer, and the source segmenter is a SimpleSegmenter; otherwise the Python prepare path runs and the resulting corpus has inverted_index=None and rust_corpus=None.

Rust prepare still runs with an embedder set when SimpleTokenizer and SimpleSegmenter are in use, so the embedding index is built on the Rust-prepared candidates; the 0.3.x skip of Rust prepare on the embedder path is gone.

align_citations and PreparedCitationCorpus.align accept a backend argument with three values: "auto" (default, try Rust then fall back), "python" (force SmithWatermanAligner), and "rust" (require RustSmithWatermanAligner, raise on construction failure).

_default_aligner constructs RustSmithWatermanAligner first under backend="auto" and falls back to SmithWatermanAligner on RuntimeError; backend="rust" propagates the RuntimeError so the caller sees a missing or mismatched extension.

When cite_right._core is missing, the same PreparedCitationCorpus API still works, but _select_candidates uses _add_lexical_candidates directly (no conjunctive rare-token intersect), max_candidates_lexical is still the cap, and pure-Python SmithWatermanAligner handles alignment including return_match_blocks for multi-span.

With an embedder on the Rust path, lexical scores are filled only for inverted-index seeds, embedding-only extras keep lexical_score == 0.0, _add_embedding_candidates may add non-index windows before Smith-Waterman, those extras still need Smith-Waterman, and retrieval_support is not a Citation and does not flip status.

The Rust inverted index uses conjunctive rare-token intersect: query tokens are sorted by posting count, the intersection of the rarest tokens is taken first, and the result is capped at max_candidates, implemented by both InvertedIndex.query and PreparedCorpus.query_index.

Rust entry points release the Python GIL via py.detach(...) during alignment, query, and citation building, and use rayon to parallelize across candidate windows and across candidates respectively, so a Python ThreadPoolExecutor can use multiple cores on the alignment hot path.

Multi-span evidence requires align_pair_blocks_details and align_batch_blocks_details on the extension; a RustSmithWatermanAligner built with return_match_blocks=True raises at construction time on an extension that does not expose them, rather than silently producing empty evidence_spans.

The Rust aligner is required to match the Python aligner exactly: same status, same char_start / char_end, same evidence, same evidence_spans when multi_span_evidence is on, same components, and same retrieval_support; deterministic tie-breaking and identical score normalization are part of the contract.
